concepts.title: Sources of Data: Primary and Secondary

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sources of Data: Primary and Secondary' refers to.
questions.a: Data for a statistical study may be collected first-hand from the field -- primary data -- or drawn from published and recorded sources -- secondary data. Primary collection gives fit and freshness at a cost; secondary use is cheap and quick but limited by someone else's purpose and definitions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sources of Data: Primary and Secondary'.
questions.a: Ask it yourself or borrow it from records -- primary costs time, secondary costs control.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sources of Data: Primary and Secondary' taught, and from which source text?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Modes of Collecting Primary Data' refers to.
questions.a: Primary data arrive by three main modes: personal interviews where the investigator questions respondents face to face; mailed questionnaires that respondents fill themselves; and telephone or telephoned interviews for quick reach. Choice depends on area, literacy, cost and accuracy needed.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Modes of Collecting Primary Data'.
questions.a: Meet, mail or phone -- each mode trades cost against accuracy and coverage.

concepts.title: Pilot Survey, Census and Sampling Frames

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Pilot Survey, Census and Sampling Frames' refers to.
questions.a: Before the main collection, a pilot survey trials the questionnaire on a small group to expose confusing questions. The study then chooses between a census -- covering every unit of the population -- and a sample survey -- studying a selected few to represent the whole; the sampling frame lists the units from which the sample is drawn.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Pilot Survey, Census and Sampling Frames'.
questions.a: Try it small, then cover all -- or let a well-chosen few speak for the whole.
